- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.11) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5% for 30-day horizon.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.22) and prices are rising, model often overshoots; cap forecast peaks at 1–2% below recent high or adjust downward by 3–5% if sentiment persists.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment, leading to delayed or exaggerated price corrections; apply lagged correction: if sentiment turns negative after a spike, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.10), model tends to forecast mean-reversion too aggressively; avoid sharp downward corrections unless sentiment confirms trend reversal.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive days of price decline after peak), reduce forecasted peak by 5–10% and shift downward slope earlier.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment followed by price recovery, model often underestimates rebound; increase forecast by 2–4% in early days of recovery if sentiment turns positive.
